# ContextMenu

Menu's panel and items, opened where they are asked for: the map's right-click menu, and a tree row's (GAP-155). A right click opens it at the pointer; a long press opens it on touch; the keyboard's context-menu key, or Shift+F10, opens it at the item that has focus. Its parts are Menu's, named `ContextMenu…`, and draw exactly as Menu's do; an item takes `external` as Menu's does.

- **Import:** `import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuCheckboxItem, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuLabel, ContextMenuPortal, ContextMenuRadioGroup, ContextMenuRadioItem, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuShortcut, ContextMenuSub, ContextMenuSubContent, ContextMenuSubTrigger, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@kozmos-ds/react";`
- **Group:** Core
- **Platforms:** React, SwiftUI and Compose; not linked to Figma yet.
- **Storybook:** <https://vodoco.github.io/kozmos-design-system/storybook/?path=/docs/navigation-contextmenu--docs>

## Example

From its `Default` story.

```tsx
import {
  ContextMenu,
  ContextMenuContent,
  ContextMenuItem,
  ContextMenuLabel,
  ContextMenuSeparator,
  ContextMenuShortcut,
  ContextMenuSub,
  ContextMenuSubContent,
  ContextMenuSubTrigger,
  ContextMenuTrigger,
  Text,
  ThemeProvider,
} from "@kozmos-ds/react";

export function ContextMenuExample() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">
      <ContextMenu>
        <ContextMenuTrigger asChild>
          <div
            tabIndex={0}
            aria-label="Gate A12, map feature"
            className="flex h-40 w-72 items-center justify-center rounded-control border border-dashed border-border focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-ring"
          >
            <Text size="sm" color="muted">
              Right click, or long press, here
            </Text>
          </div>
        </ContextMenuTrigger>
        <ContextMenuContent>
          <ContextMenuLabel>Feature actions</ContextMenuLabel>
          <ContextMenuItem>
            Copy
            <ContextMenuShortcut>⌘C</ContextMenuShortcut>
          </ContextMenuItem>
          <ContextMenuItem>
            Paste
            <ContextMenuShortcut>⌘V</ContextMenuShortcut>
          </ContextMenuItem>
          <ContextMenuSeparator />
          <ContextMenuSub>
            <ContextMenuSubTrigger>Move to level</ContextMenuSubTrigger>
            <ContextMenuSubContent>
              <ContextMenuItem>Level 1</ContextMenuItem>
              <ContextMenuItem>Level 2</ContextMenuItem>
            </ContextMenuSubContent>
          </ContextMenuSub>
          <ContextMenuItem external asChild>
            <a href="https://docs.pointr.tech">Documentation</a>
          </ContextMenuItem>
        </ContextMenuContent>
      </ContextMenu>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

## ContextMenu

Its props are `ContextMenuPrimitive.ContextMenuProps`.

- `children`: `React.ReactNode`, optional.
- `onOpenChange`: `(open: boolean) => void`, optional.
- `dir`: `Direction`, optional.
- `modal`: `boolean`, optional, default `true`.

## ContextMenuTrigger

It forwards its ref to `HTMLSpanElement`. Its props are `Omit<ContextMenuPrimitive.ContextMenuTriggerProps & React.RefAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, "ref">`.

- `asChild`: `boolean`, optional.
- `disabled`: `boolean`, optional.
- `children`: `ReactNode`, optional.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).

## ContextMenuItem

It forwards its ref to `HTMLDivElement`. Its props are `Omit<ContextMenuPrimitive.ContextMenuItemProps & React.RefAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "ref"> & MenuItemExternalProps & { inset?: boolean }`.

- `external`: `boolean`, optional.

  The item opens a page in a new tab, as Link's `external` (GAP-202,
  decision 152): the new-tab icon at the item's inline end, and
  `externalLabel` read after its name. With `asChild` around an `<a>`, the
  link gets `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, its own
  `target` and `rel` still winning; a `target` that keeps it in this tab
  (`_self`, `_parent`, `_top`) opens no new tab, so it adds none of these.
  Without `asChild`, opening the page is `onSelect`'s.

- `externalLabel`: `string`, optional.

  What a screen reader hears after the item's name when `external`:
  "Documentation opens in a new tab". English by default; pass the
  product's own words. Empty, it says nothing more.

- `inset`: `boolean`, optional.
- `onSelect`: `(event: Event) => void`, optional.
- `asChild`: `boolean`, optional.
- `disabled`: `boolean`, optional.
- `textValue`: `string`, optional.
- `children`: `ReactNode`, optional.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).
